topic: What spectral efficiency challenges arise from real-time adaptation to sparsely distributed channels in Inmarsat's BGAN signals?
consensus_response: The Inmarsat BGAN system's reliance on QPSK with 16-QAM shaping introduces higher Peak-to-Average Power Ratio (PAPR), increasing out-of-band radiation and adjacent channel interference. Real-time adaptation to sparsely distributed channels leads to reduced signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) in areas with low satellite visibility, increased interference from neighboring channels and satellites, and higher latency/packet loss rates. Optimizing the 3x3 array's design parameters, such as element spacing and phasing, can improve spectral efficiency by minimizing interference between adjacent elements.
reference_context: The Inmarsat BGAN system uses QPSK with 16-QAM shaping, which increases PAPR, reducing ERP and coverage capacity. The system also features a 3x3 array configuration with approximately 0.5λ (wavelength) spacing, leading to increased interference between adjacent elements.
